summary: Lists the accounts in a permission role, from inside a cloud function. Cloud-only and read-only — the inverse of Get User Roles.
description: Get User Roles answers 'which roles is this user in'. List Users In Role answers the other direction: 'who is in this role'. Both walk the same membership junction, and until this node existed only one direction was reachable — so 'show me the member list', the most ordinary screen in a membership app, could not be built at all except by maintaining a separate collection that duplicates the role table and goes stale the first time somebody changes a membership by hand. `Users` holds the member records in the same shape the User node reads, so a For Each over them uses the same property names. `Total` is the whole membership before `Limit`, so a clipped page is always visible as one rather than silently looking like the complete roster. `unchanged` fires when the role exists and nobody has joined it; a role that does not exist is a `failure` naming it, because answering an empty list for a misspelled role draws the empty-community screen for a typo.
whenToUse: Whenever a cloud function needs the membership of a role rather than the roles of a member — rendering a members directory or a staff list, counting how many people hold a subscription tier, or fanning a notification out to everyone in a role. Compare `Total` with the length of `Users` to decide whether to ask for another page.

ports.role: Value; required. Name of the role to list, matching the name a permission rule uses after `role:`. A blank or unusable name is a `failure`, and so is a role that does not exist.
ports.limit: Value, default 100. How many members to return in one call. Turning ids into records is one fetch each, so this is bounded rather than unlimited; `Total` still reports the whole membership.
ports.skip: Value, default 0. How many members to step over before this page — Skip 100 with Limit 100 is the second page.
ports.read: Signal (Do); performs the read. Nothing happens until this fires.
ports.treatUnchangedAs: Edit-only enum, default Unchanged. Set it to Failure if an empty role should be treated as a check failing rather than a distinct outcome.
ports.users: Value; the member records for this page, shaped like the account record /users/me answers with.
ports.userIds: Value; object ids of the members in this page, in the same order as Users.
ports.total: Value; how many members the role has in total, before Limit.
ports.done: Signal; fires once Users and User Ids hold this page of the membership.
ports.unchanged: Signal; fires when the role exists and has no members at all — the 'nobody has joined yet' branch.
ports.failure: Signal; fires when the members could not be read — a blank Role, an unusable name, or a role that does not exist.
ports.completed: Signal; fires after every attempt, whatever the outcome.
ports.error: Value; why the last attempt failed.

patterns: Put this behind a cloud function whose call rule names the role that may see the roster — a member list is other people's account records, and a cloud function runs as system, so the function's own permission rule is the only thing deciding who may read it.
Page a large role by wiring Skip from a page counter and comparing Total against the running count of rows already shown, rather than assuming one call returned everybody.
antiPatterns: Rendering Users straight onto a public page without a call rule on the function — the graph's Allow Unauthenticated port is what applies when no rule is written, and ticked means the whole membership roster is readable by anyone on the internet.
Treating the length of Users as the membership count; it is the size of one page, and Total is the number that answers 'how many members are there'.
